t: This is Hans Place, a garden square in Knightsbridge, immediately south of Harrods. It's named after Sir Hans Sloane, a physician, naturalist and collector. When he died in 1753, he left his collection of 71,000 items to the British nation. That bequest became the foundation of the British Museum, and also of the British Library and the Natural History Museum. So the square carries the name of a man whose collecting helped shape three of the country's great institutions.
